name: Haman
overview: Haman is a male figure identified as the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. His lineage connects him to the Agagites, a detail noted explicitly in Esther 3:1. The Hebrew phrase יִמַּח שְׁמוֹ, meaning 'may his name be erased,' is associated with him, reflecting a strong negative judgment within the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: Haman is known by this single proper name as recorded in Esther 3:1. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to his name in the Scripture provided.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Haman as the son of Hammedatha. Additionally, several individuals—Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha—are inferred to be his ancestors based on genealogical references in Esther 9:7-9, suggesting a detailed family lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Haman's significance in the biblical narrative arises from his identity as an Agagite and his opposition to God's people, as implied by the curse wishing his name to be erased. This reflects his role as an adversary within the story of Esther, underscoring the divine judgment pronounced against him and his lineage.
